about: Reviewed status and headline of each experiment. The research API serves the newest experiment of a study that is not superseded, with this review; artifacts themselves are git-ignored and regenerated by the commands in docs/research/results.md. Edit only after reading the experiment's metrics.json.

F1-20261021T190101Z.reason: seasonal-naive baseline repeated weeks k seasons back for horizons beyond 7 days (audit F01); baseline comparisons, champion selection and the 'trained models beat the baseline' claim are invalid

S1-20261021T193239Z.reason: replayed the defective seasonal-naive baseline (F01); its q90 policy choice was informed by the test window and is exploratory (S20)

R2-20261021T191153Z.reason: the 'temporal logic off vs on' contrast changed effective-date filtering and reranking at once (audit S13)

R2-20261022T045503Z.headline: Effective-date filtering and supersession reranking each remove wrong-version citations; together they reach 100%
R2-20261022T045503Z.notes: 2x2 factorial on 118 synthetic questions (not human-reviewed): temporal main effect +3.2 points, rerank main effect +4.2 points, interaction +0.9 points. Measures the mechanism, not real-world contract understanding.

R1-20261021T191153Z.reason: one judged test query was excluded by a qrels parsing error (DEF-04)

C1-20261021T191800Z.headline: Hybrid search finds the expert-labelled clause most often within a contract

IB-20261021T192006Z.headline: SupplyLens policy scores highest of three tool-only policies on InventoryBench
IB-20261021T192006Z.notes: Deterministic policies only; does not use the forecasting models affected by F01.

AGT-20261021T192432Z.reason: recorded before the session-4 dispatch, read-back and budget corrections

AGT-20261022T045832Z.headline: Investigator: every frozen scenario verified, zero unapproved external writes
AGT-20261022T045832Z.notes: 57 scenarios x 3 trials on the corrected code (lookup-first retry, full read-back, explicit zero budget). Deterministic control regression, not a model-capability result.

F1-20261022T090206Z.reason: the quantile TCN's weekday input channels were constant in training and inference: panel dates were reloaded in the wrong unit (Phase 5, ML-P5-01). Seasonal-naive and LightGBM results are reproduced exactly by 2.1.0

S1-20261022T092040Z.reason: its TCN rows used the weekday-blind TCN 2.0.0, and it sized orders with its own formula instead of the product's planner; S2 replays the product's actual decision logic

R1-20261022T161030Z.headline: On ACORD, vector search beats the hybrid — a negative result we keep
R1-20261022T161030Z.notes: All 57 judged test queries (one was wrongly excluded before, DEF-04); search restricted to the ACORD clause corpus. nDCG@10: vector 0.108, hybrid 0.089, lexical 0.061. Absolute scores are low and were not compared with published ACORD baselines.

F1-20261023T180239Z.headline: Trained forecasters cut daily error by about a third against seasonal naive; TCN and LightGBM are not clearly different
F1-20261023T180239Z.notes: Protocol 2.1.0 = 2.0.0 with the weekday-corrected TCN; 503 products, rolling test origins 2011-10-13 and 2011-11-10. Pooled per-product MAE: naive 21.35, LightGBM 14.52, TCN 14.32. TCN - naive -7.02 [-8.94, -5.45]; TCN - LightGBM -0.20 [-0.46, +0.03], TCN better on 42% of products (no clear difference). Not an untouched holdout (D-042).

F2-20261023T182141Z.headline: Segment-wise model choice and validation-fitted interval scaling changed nothing on this cohort
F2-20261023T182141Z.notes: Rules frozen on validation: Syntetos-Boylan classes put every product in 'lumpy' (94%) or 'erratic' (6%) at daily grain and TCN won both on validation, so the composite equals TCN; symmetric interval scaling stays at 1.0 because 39% of product-days are zero and any narrowing drops them out of the interval. Medians sum to 42-50% of realised volume (trained models). Test windows already seen.

S2-20261023T183015Z.headline: Through the product's own ordering logic, lower forecast error did not mean lower simulated cost
S2-20261023T183015Z.notes: Simulated, assumed terms and costs, 503 products, four weekly reviews 2011-11-10..2011-12-08. Unconstrained budget: a no-forecast base-stock rule cost GBP 11,983, product+naive 12,957, product+TCN 13,673 (vs naive +1.42/product [-1.64, 4.82]), product+LightGBM 19,842 (vs naive +13.69 [4.67, 25.08]). Under the workspace-scaled budget the planner rations; TCN's smaller requirements fit the budget (13,673 vs naive 78,442), an interaction with budget allocation rather than proof of forecast value.

R3-20261023T181121Z.headline: Answer-support rules flag ambiguity and some unanswerable questions, at a cost on reworded questions
R3-20261023T181121Z.notes: 535 generated questions (labels by construction, not human-reviewed), thresholds fitted on the development half. Test half, hybrid: out-of-scope abstention 0/26 -> 10/26, ambiguity 0/4 -> 3/4, answerable 45/45 kept, paraphrases answered 172/172 -> 121/172, named supplier 4/4 -> 3/4. Lexical-only (hosted demo): named supplier 4/4 -> 0/4 (false ambiguity). Retrieval-only signals cannot tell out-of-scope from reworded in-scope questions.

E1-20261026T200641Z.headline: Under a binding budget, a 5% CO2 cut is almost free (9 of 23,980 units), but halving CO2 costs 13.8 points of coverage
E1-20261026T200641Z.notes: Real UCI scope (40 SKUs, two offers each, £20,000 weekly budget); CO2 lane factors and unit weights are assumed, terms and stock simulated. Exact epsilon-constraint (CP-SAT, 21 caps, 3.1 s) against NSGA-II (pymoo, 3 seeds): NSGA-II reaches 98.1-98.5% of the exact front's hypervolume but 35-43 of its ~116 front points are dominated by exact points. The exact front is sampled at 21 caps, so its hypervolume is a lower bound.

FA1-20261026T200912Z.headline: Under a binding budget, rest-of-world customers got 51% coverage against 83% for UK customers; moderate reweighing (alpha 0.4) cuts the gap from 31.7 to 12.2 points for 1.4 points of total coverage
FA1-20261026T200912Z.notes: Real UCI scope and recorded country shares (365 days); stock, terms and budget simulated; demand is the champion forecast. A product's shortfall is attributed to its customers by past purchase share. Worst-to-best ratio 0.62 before, 0.85 at alpha 0.4 (passes the four-fifths screen). Full inverse-share reweighing (alpha 1) over-corrects: UK falls to 72% and total coverage drops 7 points. One scope, one date; deterministic allocation.

D1-20261027T053410Z.headline: On a simulated order history, a logistic risk score ranks late deliveries better than each supplier's past late rate (AUC 0.77 vs 0.69); LightGBM adds nothing (0.75)
D1-20261027T053410Z.notes: Method check only: the order history is generated from a stated process (supplier reliability, sea lanes, December peak, order size), so the models can only recover effects that were put in, and they do (sea lane and supplier carry the largest coefficients). 8,112 training and 2,392 test orders; temporal split at 2011-07-01. Real receipts from the ERP receipt feed would replace the generator.

W1-20261027T055557Z.headline: On total daily units, XGBoost beats Prophet and a seasonal naive (WAPE 24.6% vs 28.0% and 29.7%); adding London weather makes no clear difference to either (95% intervals span zero)
W1-20261027T055557Z.notes: 13 weekly origins from 2011-09-05 to 2011-11-28, 7 days ahead, 91 total-level points and 4,550 product-day points (50 products). Product-level daily demand is intermittent, so WAPE is above 100% for every model (XGBoost 110%, naive 114%) and MAPE is taken over non-zero days only. Weather on the target day is the observed value, so any gain would be an upper bound. Daily correlation of units with mean temperature -0.03 and with rainfall 0.05. Weather: Open-Meteo historical API, CC BY 4.0.

G1-20261027T054918Z.reason: ran before the product-ambiguity check, so 3 of 9 ambiguous questions were answered from one product's terms; answerable and out-of-scope results were otherwise as in the rerun

G1-20261027T061059Z.headline: All 196 generated answers kept every figure in a cited passage, with correct citations; 1 of 67 questions that should get no answer got one (3 before the product check), but the check also declines all 8 questions that name only a supplier
G1-20261027T061059Z.notes: 271 generated questions over simulated and fictional agreements (labels by construction, not human-reviewed); local qwen2.5:7b at temperature 0, median 2.8 s, p95 4.0 s. Answerable 108/108 and reworded 88/88 answered; out-of-scope 0/48 and unknown product 0/10 answered. Ambiguous: 1 of 9 answered from one product's terms (was 3 of 9). Named supplier: 0 of 8 answered (was 3 of 8) because each agreement sets terms per product, so the system asks for a product code; the labels expected an answer, so this counts as over-refusal. The figure check would pass a correct figure next to a wrong one.
